newsitem.title: USA: Universal Display shows new technology.
newsitem.headline: Universal Display shows new technology.

text.p: Universal Display Corp said it and Princeton University's Center for Photonics and Optoelectronic Materials (POEM) demonstrated in a laboratory an independently controlled, tunable, three-color organic light-emitting device, about the thickness of a dime.

It said in a statement technology is expected to permit such applications as high-definition televisions (HDTV) with flat displays that hang on walls like paintings and laptop computers with bright displays that consume considerably less energy. The results were published in the current issue of Science magazine, dated June 27, 1997.

A team of scientists at both Princeton and the University of Southern California took four years to develop the technology. The research was solely funded by Philadelphia based Universal Display, a scientific development company.
Universal said it retains exclusive licenses for the organic light-emitting diode (OLED) technology.
With less than an hour left in the trading day, Universal Display was up 3/8 at 4-1/2.
